newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-UK retailer Liberty first-half profits rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UK retailer Liberty first-half profits rise.

text.p: Liberty Plc, the British retailer known for its fine fabrics, on Friday reported an increase in first-half pretax profits and said the results demonstrate that it will continue to deliver on promises it made in its restructuring programme.
Pretax profits for the first half ended July 27 rose to 1.09 million pounds ($1.70 million) from 280,000 pounds a year earlier. Turnover edged down to 39.03 million pounds from 39.27 million.
Liberty's shares rose 15 pence to 435p on the London Stock Exchange following the release of results.

"We have done precisely what we said we would do and have given a clear indication that the rest of the year will give more of what we promised," chairman Denis Cassidy told Reuters in a phone interview.

"The thing to bear in mind in this first half is the figures to the 27th of July include only two months of the clearing up," Cassidy said. "Virtually the whole programme will be completed by the end of the trading year, certainly within the first quarter of 1997," he added.
Liberty said the restructuring provisions it established will be adequate for the entire programme.
As of July 27, Liberty had used six million pounds of the total 18 million pound provision, Cassidy said.
Managing director Ian Thomson said results will continue to improve as the new management team is able to implement its merchandising strategy. The new management team took over in April.
"You'll appreciate in the retail business when you arrive in April you're looking at merchandise that's been bought for the summer season and largely for the winter," Thomson said.

"The management we've put in place is working on spring/summer 1997," he said. "I think we can see some reasonable signs of improvement in Christmas," he added. "But we would be looking at improvements for 1997."

Liberty is investigating ways to expand its sales space at its flagship Regent Street store in London and in November will open a new men's clothing department in the basement using 12,000 square feet of additional space that it is turning into selling area.

Liberty, which has always been low key in promoting itself to the public, is planning on taking a stronger message to the public, including an advertising campaign. Thomson declined to provide details of the planned advertising campaign.

In addition the company is continuing to build on its airport shops. It now has four shops at London's Heathrow airport, which Cassidy said play a key role in promoting the Liberty brand to consumers and acting as a bridge to carry it outside Britain.
